title: Network commissioning: register 40101
summary: The documentation says registers 40101-40102. Somebody entered 101. Find out what the PLC actually asks for.
objectives: Diagnose Modbus TCP communication from network evidence
Compare the configuration with the device documentation
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed. *)
    LevelHighHigh : BOOL; (* High-high level switch: TRUE when wet. *)
    LevelPermille : INT; (* LT-401 level, per mille, over Modbus TCP. *)
    LevelCommOK : BOOL; (* LT-401 connection exchanges data. *)
    LevelLitres : REAL; (* LI-402 level in litres through gateway GW-402. *)
    GatewayCommOK : BOOL; (* LI-402 connection exchanges data. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-404. *)
    DrainPump : BOOL; (* Drain pump P-405. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from LT-401, 0..100 %. *)
    CheckPercent : REAL; (* Level from LI-402: litres of a 100 litre tank. *)
    CommAlarm : BOOL; (* A level connection does not exchange data. *)
    DeviationAlarm : BOOL; (* The two levels differ by more than 5 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Filling : BOOL; (* Fill request latch. *)
END_VAR
(* The program passed its factory test; this lab is about the network and its configuration. *)
LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelPermille) / 10.0;
CheckPercent := LevelLitres;
CommAlarm := NOT (LevelCommOK AND GatewayCommOK);
DeviationAlarm := (LevelPercent - CheckPercent > 5.0) OR (CheckPercent - LevelPercent > 5.0);
Filling := (StartPB OR Filling) AND StopPB AND NOT CommAlarm AND NOT DeviationAlarm AND NOT LevelHighHigh AND LevelPercent < 80.0;
InletValve := Filling;
DrainPump := FALSE;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: The PLC runs the accepted program. Let the simulation run and press Start; confirm the symptom.
Open the Network view: nodes, connections, the selected connection's request and response, and the traffic.
Compare the configuration with the device documentation in the scene description; use ping.
Diagnose, correct (configuration labs: Advanced mode, then download) or repair, then verify.
hints: Look at what the PLC sends and what comes back, message by message.
A fast exception, a timeout and no route mean very different things.

scenarios.title: Communicate, start filling and reach the setpoint

criteria.title: Both level connections exchange data
criteria.onFail: A level connection did not exchange data (CommAlarm).

criteria.title: Both levels agree with the tank
criteria.onFail: LevelPercent and CheckPercent were not about 20 % while the tank held 20 %.

troubleshooting.symptom: The tank does not fill. The gateway answers every request with an exception.

diagnosisOptions.label: The LT-401 connection uses the wrong IP address
The LI-402 connection uses the wrong unit ID
The LI-402 connection's timeout is shorter than the gateway needs
The LI-402 REAL value is decoded with the wrong word order
The LI-402 connection reads the wrong registers
The PLC network cable is unplugged

debrief.rootCause: The connection read from protocol address 101. The documentation's registers 40101-40102 are protocol addresses 100-101 in the 4xxxx convention, so the read started one register late and ran past the device's register map, which the gateway answered with exception 02h (illegal data address).
evidence: Every request was answered with exception 02h.
The request started at protocol address 101.
In the 4xxxx notation, 40101 is protocol address 100.
debrief.repair: Set the start address to 100, download, and verify the value.
debrief.reasoning: Always translate the manual's register numbers into the zero-based protocol address the PLC sends, and check which convention the manual uses.
